agent_executive_summary: Investment batch of 15, 5-7yr hold. No Strong Buys. One Buy: Smart Suites (D14) — freehold efficient 2BR, 260m to Aljunied MRT, ~10% below URA median at a liquid $1.25M. Three Avoids: 27 Lor 32 Geylang (overpriced unproven boutique new-build), The Ramford (14% above median on 6 txns), and — borderline — these are the clear no-buys. The Clement Canopy, Le Quest, and The Tre Ver are the most data-reliable Neutrals (143/118/295 txns) but all priced at fair value with modest appreciation. The remainder are Neutral: fully-priced central-fringe freeholds (Ava Towers, iResidences, One Leicester), oversized/niche 4BR ECs in OCR (Twin Waterfalls, Watercolours, Heron Bay), and low-quantum value/yield plays with data gaps (Flora View, Mar Thoma Rd, Pavilion Square).
agent_market_commentary: June 2026: ABSD and the elevated-rate regime keep the deepest liquidity in the $1.5-2.5M band; sub-$1.3M efficient 2BRs near MRT (Smart Suites) and integrated/quality developments retain the broadest exit. 4BR units above $1.9M consistently face thin, family-only resale pools and should be approached with a discount. Small-sample URA rates (One Leicester 11%/22txn, Ava Towers 8.1%/20txn, The Ramford -0.3%/6txn) must be discounted heavily — they distort the algorithm's appreciation inputs.
agent_methodology_notes: Rated each listed unit type at its listed price/PSF for an investment hold. Web-verified two ambiguous cases: One Leicester (recent txns $1,602-$2,013 psf — asking is top-of-range) and Heron Bay (privatised EC, 394 units, recent $1,202-$1,557 psf — asking mid-range). Could not verify: Twin Waterfalls, 27 Lor 32 Geylang, Flora View, Mar Thoma Rd, Watercolours all lack URA appreciation/txn data (rated conservatively). Treated oversized layouts (Twin Waterfalls 2,174sqft, Mar Thoma 1,410sqft, Watercolours/Heron Bay large 4BRs) as psf-flattering, not value. Discounted all <30-txn CAGRs.
